addresses.name: ConsoleCmd_DetailedLog
addresses.comment: **The `detailedlog` / `dl` console command** ('Prints detailed log of entire game data (use for debugging).', argument 'FilePathAndName'). No argument: 'Please specify file path and name.'. Otherwise builds `logs/<name>.log` and hands it with the game state to 0x68C650 - a writer that opens a VirtualFile and emits SaveWriteKey/SaveWriteValue pairs, so a save-shaped dump of the game state (inferred; 0x68C650 not read past its first calls) - and answers 'See <path> for result.'. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-console.md.
addresses.evidence: Its row in the command table (VA 0x170AF88 + 0x4C*0; name pointer at +4, handler at +0x1C = VA 0x170AFA4) names it, and the reply strings it pushes are the command's own. The table is walked by ConsoleCommands_Fill (0x444150 `mov ebx,0x170AF88` ... `add ebx,0x4C; cmp ebx,0x170BF44`), so a handler pointer there is an entry; bare `ret` checked by checkSignatures. Would be wrong if the row's +0x1C were not the handler - but Execute calls exactly [row+0x1C] (0x4443E4 `mov ecx,[eax+0x1C]; call ecx`).

See also reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weathersim.md, section A. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-console.md.

addresses.name: ConsoleCmd_Debug
addresses.comment: **The `debug <word>` console command** ('Various debugging actions'; its argument text lists the 15 words), one function 0x441520..0x442578 that compares the first argument against literals in turn, exactly and case-sensitively. `info`, `profile`, `log_profile` flip bits 0x2000000, 0x800000, 0x400000 of GameSettings +0xEC (each also copies bit 0 into render_trees +0xE4); `tooltips` flips g_TooltipsEnabled; `assert` flips g_AssertsEnabled; `textures` writes the graphics' texture list to the log; `fow` flips g_FogOfWarEnabled and asks the in-game screen for a whole map refresh (+0x84 = -1, -1 pushed on +0x88); `nopopup` flips g_NoPopups; `spy` g_SpyCheat; `yesmen` g_AiYesmen; `wireframe` flips g_ConsoleWireframe, mirrors it to graphics +0x6BC44 and sets D3DRS_FILLMODE to wireframe/solid; `minzoom N` sets MapCamera +0x35C lowest_height_setting to N where N > 0; `render` alone prints the ten layer bits of +0xF0 AND +0xEC, `render <LAYER>` (upper-cased with CharUpperBuffA) flips one of TREES 0x1, BORDERS 0x2, TEXT 0x8, OVERLAY 0x10, OBJECTS 0x20, MAPOBJECTS 0x40, RIVERS 0x80, WATER 0x100, WATERBORDERS 0x200, EFFECTS 0x400 in +0xEC; `color TAG r g b` (0..255 each, divided by 255.0) sets a country's map colour (0x4CCD00) and refreshes the map; `save TAG` calls 0x4F5730, 'Country color saved'. No argument: 'Please specify some arguments.'; an unknown word: an empty reply. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-console.md.
addresses.evidence: Its row in the command table (VA 0x170AF88 + 0x4C*43; name pointer at +4, handler at +0x1C = VA 0x170BC68) names it, and the reply strings it pushes are the command's own. The table is walked by ConsoleCommands_Fill (0x444150 `mov ebx,0x170AF88` ... `add ebx,0x4C; cmp ebx,0x170BF44`), so a handler pointer there is an entry; bare `ret` checked by checkSignatures. Would be wrong if the row's +0x1C were not the handler - but Execute calls exactly [row+0x1C] (0x4443E4 `mov ecx,[eax+0x1C]; call ecx`). The literals are pushed in this order at 0x441643 (info) ... 0x4423F9 (save); the help row's argument text at VA 0x170BC74 lists the same 15 words and no reading found a 16th. A single frame (`and esp,-8`, one SEH record) and one exit at 0x442578 - the `function starts at 0x441A0E` that findRefs reports is the heuristic, not an entry.

addresses.evidence: Its row in the command table (VA 0x170AF88 + 0x4C*52; name pointer at +4, handler at +0x1C = VA 0x170BF14) names it, and the reply strings it pushes are the command's own. The table is walked by ConsoleCommands_Fill (0x444150 `mov ebx,0x170AF88` ... `add ebx,0x4C; cmp ebx,0x170BF44`), so a handler pointer there is an entry; bare `ret` checked by checkSignatures. Would be wrong if the row's +0x1C were not the handler - but Execute calls exactly [row+0x1C] (0x4443E4 `mov ecx,[eax+0x1C]; call ecx`).

addresses.name: ConsoleCommands_Fill
addresses.no_signature: The vector to fill in EAX (`mov esi,eax`), no stack arguments, bare `ret` - a register convention no signature expresses.
addresses.comment: **Fills the console's vector of command pointers from the static table.** Empties the vector (EAX), reserves 0x35 = 53 (VectorOfPointers_Reserve), then pushes a pointer to each 0x4C-byte row from VA 0x170AF88 while the row pointer is below VA 0x170BF44 - which is what fixes the table at 53 rows. One caller, the console's constructor at 0x60C3A4, on the console's +0x48. 0x444110..0x4441C9. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-console.md.
addresses.evidence: 0x444142 `push 0x35; call VectorOfPointers_Reserve`, 0x444150 `mov ebx,0x170AF88`, 0x4441B8 `add ebx,0x4C`, 0x4441BB `cmp ebx,0x170BF44; jl`. (0x170BF44-0x170AF88)/0x4C = 53 exactly, and the bytes at 0x170BF44 (0x102, then a null name pointer) are no row. Wrong if a second walker used another bound - findValue finds 0x170AF88 and 0x170BF44 once each in .text.

addresses.name: ConsoleCommands_Find
addresses.no_signature: The command vector in ECX and the typed word (a std::string*) on the stack, `ret 4`, answering the row or null: a __thiscall on a std::vector, with no class in the record to carry the `::`.
addresses.comment: **Finds a console command by name or alias.** For each row pointer in the vector: an exact, case-sensitive byte compare of the word with the row's name (+4), then with each of its +8 aliases (+0xC..); the first row that matches is answered, else 0. Callers: ConsoleCommands_Execute and ConsoleCommands_DescribeOne. 0x4441D0..0x4442CB. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-console.md.
addresses.evidence: Read whole: 0x444216 `mov ecx,[esi+4]` and the two-byte compare loop, 0x444249 `mov edi,[esi+8]` and the alias loop from `esi+0xC`; three exits all `ret 4`. No tolower/toupper call anywhere in it.

addresses.name: ConsoleCommands_Execute
addresses.no_signature: The command vector in ECX (passed straight on to ConsoleCommands_Find), the reply out and the vector of tokens on the stack, `ret 8`, answering the reply: a __thiscall on a std::vector.
addresses.comment: **Runs one console line.** Finds tokens[0] (ConsoleCommands_Find): none - 'Unknown command'; a row whose first byte is 0 - 'Command available only for developers.' (rows `weather` and `crash`); a row with no handler (+0x1C) - 'Console Error - command has missing action.'. Otherwise copies tokens[1..] into a fresh vector and calls handler(&reply, &args), __cdecl, then copies the reply's success byte and text out. One caller, Console_SubmitLine (0x60C956). 0x4442D0..0x4444CD. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-console.md.
addresses.evidence: 0x44431A `cmp byte [eax],0; jne` with the developers string pushed on the fall-through, 0x44433F `cmp [eax+0x1C],edi; je` to the missing-action string, 0x4443E4 `mov ecx,[eax+0x1C]; call ecx; add esp,8`. Tokens are 0x1C-byte strings (the 0x92492493 divide). No global is consulted for the developer test, so no build-time switch can enable those two rows.

addresses.name: ConsoleCommands_DescribeOne
addresses.no_signature: The command vector in ECX, the reply out and the word on the stack, `ret 8`: a __thiscall on a std::vector.
addresses.comment: **`help <command>`'s text.** ConsoleCommands_Find on the word; found: ConsoleCommand_Format's line, '\n - ' and the description (+0x18); not found: 'Command not found'. It does not test the row's developer byte. 0x4444D0..0x444630. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-console.md.
addresses.evidence: 0x4444F6 call ConsoleCommands_Find, 0x444506 `mov edi,[esi+0x18]`, 0x44453D the ' - ' string, 0x444611 'Command not found'; exits `ret 8`. No read of [esi] (the developer byte) between the find and the format.

addresses.name: ConsoleCommands_ListAll
addresses.comment: **`help` and `helplog`'s list.** Clears `out`, then for every row pointer in `commands` whose first byte is set appends ConsoleCommand_Format's line - so the two developer-only rows are left out. Callers: ConsoleCmd_HelpLog and ConsoleCmd_Help. `ret 8`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-console.md.
addresses.evidence: 0x44465C `mov ebx,[ebp+8]` (the vector), 0x444660 `mov esi,[ebp+0xC]` (the out string, initialised empty at 0x444669), 0x444693 `cmp byte [eax],0; je` skips the row, 0x44469D ConsoleCommand_Format; `ret 8` at 0x44470A.

addresses.name: ConsoleCommand_Format
addresses.comment: **One console command as `help` shows it**: the name, then `(alias,alias)` where there are aliases, then ` [arg]` for each of the +0x20 argument texts (+0x24..). Callers: ConsoleCommands_ListAll, ConsoleCommands_DescribeOne and a third. 0x43A380 to the bare `ret` at 0x43A598. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-console.md.
addresses.evidence: Strings '(' ',' ')' ' [' ']' at VA 0x15B6C90..0x15B6CA0 appended in that structure; reads +4, +8, +0xC.., +0x20, +0x24..; callers clean 8 bytes (`add esp,8` at 0x444561 and 0x4446A2).

addresses.name: Console_SubmitLine
addresses.no_signature: The console (CInGameIdler +0x1CC4) in ECX, no stack arguments, bare `ret` - a __thiscall whose class has no RTTI name, so there is nothing to put before a `::`.
addresses.comment: **What Enter in the console does.** Takes the edit box's (+0x28) text, TrimWhitespace, keeps it in the history and console_history.txt, then: **where the in-game screen's +0x68 (multiplayer) is set, prints 'No cheats in MP' and runs nothing** - for every command, help included. Otherwise splits the line on spaces (0xA5B520, 0x20), calls ConsoleCommands_Execute on the console's command vector (+0x48), splits the reply on newlines and prints each line prefixed with §W where the reply's success byte is set and §R where it is not. Installed as a callback at 0x60BF2C (no direct caller). 0x60C640..0x60CC57. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-console.md.
addresses.evidence: 0x60C8BB `mov eax,[eax+0xBE8]; cmp byte [eax+0x68],bl; je` with 'No cheats in MP' on the fall-through; 0x60C927 `push 0x20` ... call 0xA5B520; 0x60C952 `mov ecx,[ecx+0x48]` ... call 0x4442D0; 0x60C97E/0x60C98C pick VA 0x15B6700 (§W) or 0x15B5C58 (§R) on the reply byte. Its only reference is the pointer written at 0x60BF2C. That +0x1CC4 is the console comes from CInGameIdler_HandleInput (0x6535D4), which sends the arrow keys to the history functions 0x60C540/0x60C580 when +0x1CC4's +0x30 is set.

addresses.name: g_ConsoleCommandTable
addresses.comment: **The console's command table: 53 rows of ConsoleCommandDef (0x4C bytes each), VA 0x170AF88 to 0x170BF44**, initialised in the image. Row 0 is `detailedlog`, row 52 `help`; rows 21 (`weather`) and 50 (`crash`) carry a 0 first byte and are refused as developer-only. The VA 0x170B498 earlier comments cite is row 17's name field (`noneutrality`), not the start. ConsoleCommands_Fill copies pointers to every row into the console's vector. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-console.md.
addresses.evidence: Bounds from ConsoleCommands_Fill's two constants and its reserve of 0x35; every one of the 53 rows has a name pointer into .rdata and a handler pointer into .text 0x43A6B0..0x443E90, and the dword before row 0 (VA 0x170AF84, 1.0f) and the row-sized block after the end (0x102, null name) do not parse as rows. A scan of every non-code section for pointers to the handler block found none outside the table (positive control: all 53 table pointers found).

addresses.name: g_InstantConstruction
addresses.no_signature: A global byte, not a function.
addresses.comment: **The `instantconstruction` / `instantproduction` / `inc` console cheat.** One byte, zero-initialised (.bss). Flipped only by ConsoleCmd_InstantConstruction (0x43FFF2..0x43FFFF); its one reader is CDistributeProduction::Distribute at 0x51A1C5, where a line whose progress (+0x38) is below its duration (+0x34) is still offered to slot 9 to finish. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-console.md.
addresses.evidence: findValue: three references in .text - 0x43FFF4 and 0x440000 (the handler's test and `sete` store) and 0x51A1C7 (`cmp byte [0x1A8559A],0; je` after `cmp [ebx+0x38],eax; jge`).

addresses.name: g_AssertsEnabled
addresses.no_signature: A global byte, not a function.
addresses.comment: **`debug assert`'s switch.** One byte, 1 in the image's .data. Flipped by ConsoleCmd_Debug (0x441788..0x4417B4: 'Asserts are now turned OFF.' / 'ON.'); one other reader at VA 0xA5A104, inside a function whose entry was not established (an assert reporter, by the name - inferred). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-console.md.
addresses.evidence: image.read(VA 0x17098E2) = 01; findRefs --address: four references, three in the debug handler and 0xA5A104. What the fourth does with it was not read, hence inferred for the name.

addresses.name: g_ConsoleWireframe
addresses.no_signature: A global byte, not a function.
addresses.comment: **`debug wireframe`'s switch.** One byte, zero (.bss). The handler flips it, copies it to the graphics' (0x1A857CC) byte +0x6BC44 and calls the device's (+0x64) slot 57 with (8, 2) or (8, 3) - SetRenderState(D3DRS_FILLMODE, WIREFRAME / SOLID) - 'Wireframe ON' / 'Wireframe OFF'. No reader outside the handler. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-console.md.
addresses.evidence: findRefs --address 0x1BEA3FC: three references, all at 0x441A1B..0x441A4F in ConsoleCmd_Debug. D3DRS_FILLMODE is 8 and D3DFILL_WIREFRAME/SOLID 2/3 in d3d9types.h; slot 57 being SetRenderState is the IDirect3DDevice9 layout (0xE4/4), consistent with the record's other device calls.

addresses.name: g_ConsoleOpenWindow
addresses.no_signature: A global pointer, not a function.
addresses.comment: **The window the `window open` console command made last** (a gui object, null at start). `open` destroys the old one (slot 20) before making the next, `close` destroys it and clears the pointer. Only ConsoleCmd_Window touches it. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-console.md.
addresses.evidence: findRefs --address 0x1BEA3F8: five references, all in ConsoleCmd_Window (0x43B009..0x43B0E4).

addresses.name: g_log_command_execution
addresses.comment: byte. When non-zero, Session::PumpCommands writes 'Executing command ' <type id> <serial> to the log for every command it runs (tested at rva 0x689855). **Set to 1 - never cleared - by the `randomlog` console command** (ConsoleCmd_RandomLog, `mov byte [0x1A857BE],1` at 0x43B1A7, 'Random Logging started'), although its help text says it toggles. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-console.md and reversing/findings/FINDINGS-commands.md.
addresses.evidence: 0x43B1A7 `mov byte ptr [0x1A857BE], 1` in the handler of table row 5 (`randomlog`). That no other writer exists rests on findValue over .text, which returns the handler's store and the PumpCommands test.
addresses.revises: the old comment said what sets it was not found: the `randomlog` console command does, one-way; confidence raised to confirmed.

structs.name: ConsoleCommandDef
structs.comment: **One row of the console's static command table** (g_ConsoleCommandTable, 53 of them). No RTTI and no vftable; the name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-console.md.
structs.evidence: Stride 0x4C from ConsoleCommands_Fill (`add ebx,0x4C`); each field read by ConsoleCommands_Find, ConsoleCommands_Execute and ConsoleCommand_Format as listed on the fields.

structs.name: ConsoleReply
structs.comment: **What a console handler fills**: a success byte and a std::string. The console prints the text §W when the byte is set and §R when not. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-console.md.
structs.evidence: Every handler writes `mov byte [out],0|1` and builds a std::string at out+4 (+0x14 cap 0xF, +0x10 size 0); ConsoleCommands_Execute copies [eax] and [eax+4] out; std::string is 0x1C, so 0x20.

struct_fields.name: available_in_release
struct_fields.comment: 1 on 51 rows, 0 on `weather` and `crash`: ConsoleCommands_Execute refuses a 0 row with 'Command available only for developers.' and ConsoleCommands_ListAll leaves it out of `help`.

struct_fields.name: name
struct_fields.comment: The command word, matched exactly and case-sensitively.
struct_fields.evidence: 0x444216 `mov ecx,[esi+4]` before the compare loop in ConsoleCommands_Find.

struct_fields.name: alias_count
struct_fields.comment: How many of the three alias slots are used (0..2 in the table).
struct_fields.evidence: 0x444249 `mov edi,[esi+8]` bounds the alias loop; row 35 has 2.

struct_fields.name: aliases
struct_fields.comment: Alternative words; unused slots are null or the empty string at VA 0x15B4945.
struct_fields.evidence: 0x444252 `add esi,0xC` and the loop's `add esi,4`; 0x18 - 0xC = three slots before the description.

struct_fields.name: handler
struct_fields.comment: ConsoleReply* __cdecl (ConsoleReply* out, std::vector<std::string>* args) - the arguments without the command word.
struct_fields.evidence: 0x44433F null test and 0x4443E4 `mov ecx,[eax+0x1C]; call ecx; add esp,8`.

struct_fields.name: argument_count
struct_fields.comment: How many argument texts follow (0..5 in the table).

struct_fields.name: arguments
struct_fields.comment: The argument descriptions `help` prints in brackets; ten slots fill the row to 0x4C.

struct_fields.name: ok
struct_fields.evidence: Console_SubmitLine 0x60C983 picks the colour on this byte.

struct_fields.name: text
struct_fields.comment: The reply; split on newlines when printed.
struct_fields.evidence: Every handler's `lea ecx,[out+4]` std::string initialisation; 0x60C971 splits it on 0x0A.

struct_fields.name: infra_painting
struct_fields.comment: Flipped by the console command `ipaint` (ConsoleCmd_InfraPaint, 'Now painting infra. Shift-click to pick up, click to paint.'). A map editor's switch beside +0x5/+0x6/+0x8; its readers were not looked for. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-console.md.
struct_fields.evidence: 0x43D1C9 `cmp byte [eax+7],bl; sete cl; mov [eax+7],cl` with eax = CCurrentGameState +0xBE8.

struct_fields.name: console
struct_fields.comment: The console object (no RTTI class): its +0x28 is the input edit box, +0x30 whether it is open, +0x44 the history cursor, +0x48 the vector of ConsoleCommandDef pointers ConsoleCommands_Fill makes. CInGameIdler_HandleInput sends the up and down arrows to its history while it is open. The layout of the object beyond those is not read. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-console.md.
struct_fields.evidence: 0x6535D4 `mov esi,[ebx+0x1CC4]; mov al,[esi+0x30]` in CInGameIdler_HandleInput, then the history functions 0x60C540/0x60C580 with ESI = it, which use +0x28, +0x34, +0x3C and +0x44; Console_SubmitLine reads +0x28 and +0x48. That the object is the same one whose +0x48 the constructor fills (0x60C3A1) is inferred from the shared offsets.

struct_fields.name: multiplayer
struct_fields.comment: Zero in single player; the autosave decision branches on it. **The console tests its low byte before running any line and answers 'No cheats in MP' where it is set** (Console_SubmitLine, 0x60C8C1) - which is what makes the name more than a guess. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-console.md.
struct_fields.evidence: 0x60C8BB `mov eax,[eax+0xBE8]; cmp byte [eax+0x68],bl; je` with the 'No cheats in MP' string on the fall-through.
struct_fields.revises: comment only: adds the console's 'No cheats in MP' test as the evidence the old comment lacked ('apparently multiplayer (untested)'); name and type unchanged.

struct_fields.name: layer_mask_ec
struct_fields.comment: ANDed with +0xF0 by the renderer. 0xFFFF from the constructor; CSettingsScreen::StoreChoices sets or clears bit 0 with renderTrees. **The console also writes it**: `debug render <LAYER>` flips one of bits 0x1..0x400 by name (TREES 0x1, BORDERS 0x2, TEXT 0x8, OVERLAY 0x10, OBJECTS 0x20, MAPOBJECTS 0x40, RIVERS 0x80, WATER 0x100, WATERBORDERS 0x200, EFFECTS 0x400), and `debug info`, `debug profile` and `debug log_profile` flip 0x2000000, 0x800000 and 0x400000 (each also copying bit 0 into render_trees +0xE4). So in a game nobody has typed into, the other bits - the province names' 0x8 among them - follow the map mode's +0xF0 alone. Readers of the three high bits were not looked for. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-console.md and reversing/findings/FINDINGS-farmap.md.
struct_fields.evidence: xor dword [eax+0xEC] with 1, 2, 8, esi(0x10), 0x20, 0x40, 0x80, 0x100, 0x200, 0x400 at 0x441EBD..0x44208E, and with 0x2000000 / 0x800000 / 0x400000 at 0x441676, 0x4416F0, 0x4417D6, each after GetGameSettings.
struct_fields.revises: comment only: it said only bit 0 is ever changed; the console's `debug` command flips ten layer bits and three high bits of it.
